0b8369b5.task:
Perform comprehensive black-box reconnaissance and attack-surface mapping of https://vault.kervia.ch ONLY. Do NOT test any other domain, IP, service, or port.

Scope surfaces to map:
- REST API /v1/* (Bearer "av_" keys)
- MCP endpoint /mcp
- Admin webui /ui/* and /admin/* (session cookie)
- First-boot setup /setup/*

Tasks:
1. Establish baseline connectivity and TLS/server fingerprinting (banner, headers, HTTP/2, server tech, framework hints).
2. Enumerate routes/endpoints across the above surfaces using directory/file discovery (ffuf, dirsearch, katana) and JS analysis. Map HTTP methods, parameters, and response codes for each discovered path. Keep crawls bounded (depth/duration) and clean up raw wordlist output after extracting endpoints.
3. Fetch and analyze JavaScript bundles/static assets for API endpoint references, hidden paths, config, and client-side logic (especially setup wizard, admin UI, MCP client).
4. Map the authentication model observed externally: how /v1/* Bearer av_ keys are expected, how /ui/* session cookie works, what /setup/* exposes pre-provisioning.
5. Identify technology/framework versions (headers, error pages, generator meta, JS libs, retire-style checks).

IMPORTANT constraints:
- NO credentials provided. Unauthenticated observation and mapping ONLY.
- Do NOT brute-force anything (rate limits are intentional).
- Do NOT send injection/exploit payloads — that is for later hunting agents. You map the surface and observe default behavior (status codes, redirects, error messages, JSON shapes).
- Record every endpoint you discover into shared notes (a living endpoint inventory) with method, path, params, and observed behavior.
- Record coverage entries for each surface you map.

Deliver: a written endpoint/tech inventory in shared notes, plus a concise summary of the attack surface, auth model, and any notable observations (e.g. verbose errors, exposed setup state, missing controls).

b6e79d5b.task:
Deep-test the authentication and recovery flows of https://vault.kervia.ch ONLY. No other domain/IP/port. No credentials available; unauthenticated auth-bypass and logic-flaw testing only. DO NOT brute-force (rate limits intentional) — but you MAY test response oracles, format validation, and logic flaws with a small number of crafted requests (single-digit attempts per variant), not enumeration.

Read the shared note 7d5ec8 (endpoint inventory) and get_threat_model first. Focus areas:

1. POST /recovery/recover {code, new_password} — the highest-value surface. It reaches the handler WITHOUT a session (returns invalid_code, not unauthorized). Determine:
   - Whether the code parameter is validated in a way that leaks validity (distinct error messages/timing/status for invalid vs malformed vs valid-format codes).
   - Whether new_password is accepted/applied in any state (e.g. empty code, null code, type confusion, missing field) — i.e. can you reset the admin password without a valid code?
   - Code format: length, charset, casing (uppercase), single-use semantics — observe, do NOT enumerate.
   - Whether there's any way to derive or bypass the code (e.g. code in response, code length revealed, predictable generation).
2. POST /admin/login {password} — session handling. Test for account/state leakage in error responses, timing, and any auth-bypass (empty password, type confusion, extra fields).
3. Session cookie: attributes (HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite), fixation, logout behavior, whether session is predictable.
4. Bearer "av_" key validation on /v1/whoami — test header parsing/confusion (e.g. "av_" prefix truncation, empty/partial keys, case handling) to see if key validation has a logic flaw, WITHOUT brute force.
5. /setup/info disclosure (internal mesh IP 100.100.108.242:8321 + version) — assess severity; confirm it's public and note what it leaks. This is an information-disclosure finding candidate (likely low/medium).

For any CONFIRMED vulnerability, build a working PoC and file it with create_vulnerability_report (you are authorized to report). Run the counterevidence pass and set confidence honestly. Record coverage for every surface you test (reuse/update existing entries from recon where present — check list_coverage first). Use notes for durable facts.

Deliver: findings (filed reports) + coverage + a summary of what was ruled out vs left as open proof gaps.

cf157082.task:
Test the REST API (/v1/*) and MCP (/mcp) of https://vault.kervia.ch for auth-bypass and injection. ONLY this host. No credentials; unauthenticated testing only. Do NOT brute-force keys or send volume fuzzing against rate-limited endpoints — a small number of crafted requests per vector only.

Read shared note 7d5ec8 and get_threat_model first. Both /v1/* and /mcp are 401-gated unauthenticated. Your job is to find any way to bypass that gate or reach handler logic without a valid av_ key:

1. Auth bypass on /v1/* and /mcp: HTTP method tampering (GET/POST/HEAD/OPTIONS/PUT/PATCH), header confusion (Authorization: Bearer with empty/partial/"av_" prefix variants, X-Forwarded-* spoofing to look internal, multiple auth headers), path/verb case variations, and any endpoint that accidentally skips auth middleware. Test a handful of variants, not a fuzz campaign.
2. Injection on unauthenticated-reachable inputs: the only pre-auth inputs are /recovery/recover {code,new_password} and /admin/login {password} — but those belong to another agent (Auth & Recovery). On your surfaces, test injection where any input is reachable before 401 (query params on /v1/secrets?vault=, MCP initialize/JSON-RPC body if it reaches the handler pre-auth). Look for reflected input, error-based SQLi hints, template injection, and JSON parsing behavior that reaches the app before auth.
3. IDOR/BOLA: /v1/secrets?vault=<name> and /admin/secrets id/vault params are the IDOR candidates, but require a valid key/session. Without credentials, confirm they are properly 401-gated and record the access-control surface as needs_follow_up (proof gap: no credentials). Do not mark them ruled_out.
4. Confirm rate limiting (429) behavior is consistent and note it (not a finding — it's a control).

For any CONFIRMED vulnerability, build a PoC and file via create_vulnerability_report. Run counterevidence pass; set confidence honestly. Record coverage for each surface (check list_coverage first and update existing entries rather than duplicating).

Deliver: findings + coverage + summary of ruled-out vs open proof gaps.

97043740.task:
Test the admin web UI and template surface of https://vault.kervia.ch ONLY. No other domain/IP/port. No credentials; unauthenticated testing only. Do NOT brute-force or volume-fuzz against rate-limited endpoints.

Read shared note 7d5ec8 and get_threat_model first. Two surfaces remain under-covered:

1. /admin/* route auth-bypass (mirror of what was done on /v1/*): the admin routes (agents, vaults, secrets, grants, audit, settings, templates, recovery, update, password) are all session-cookie gated (401 unauthenticated). Test for auth-gate bypass with a small number of crafted requests per vector — HTTP method tampering, header spoofing (X-Forwarded-For/Host/X-Real-IP), path/case variation, and any route that accidentally skips the session middleware. Confirm the gate is uniform (no differential/reflection/parse-error leakage).

2. /ui/* public SPA + template validation: 
   - The /ui/* SPA is public (login page). Fetch and analyze the SPA for client-side issues: DOM-based XSS sinks, prototype pollution (object merge in JS bundle), client-side path traversal, postMessage handlers, and any unsafe use of URL params/hash/localStorage. The bundle is /ui/assets/index-CrU8J1K5.js (~560KB).
   - "Template validation" (from scope) — the app manages secret templates (POST /admin/templates, ~58 templates). These are session-gated, but check whether template data is ever reflected/rendered client-side in a way that enables stored/reflected XSS, and whether the templates endpoint leaks template content unauthenticated.
   - Test reflected content on /ui/* (query/hash) for reflected XSS/HTML injection.

3. Note the admin UI's self-reported version and any verbose client-side error handling that leaks internals.

For any CONFIRMED vulnerability, build a PoC and file with create_vulnerability_report. Run the counterevidence pass; set confidence honestly. Record coverage for each surface (check list_coverage first; update existing entries, don't duplicate). No valid session/key means object-level authz on /admin/* stays needs_follow_up (proof gap) — do not mark ruled_out.

Deliver: findings + coverage + summary of ruled-out vs open proof gaps.
